content: 1. Degiacomi et al. conducted an in vitro study to investigate bedaquiline resistance in multidrug-resistant clinical isolates of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Microbiology in 2020. 2. Shi et al. explored spontaneous mutational patterns and identified novel mutations associated with resistance to bedaquiline and clofazimine in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Microbiology Spectrum in 2023. 3. Snobre et al. provided further insights into resistance mechanisms in Mycobacterium tuberculosis mutants selected for bedaquiline and clofazimine resistance, emphasizing the role of the Rv0678 gene. Their work appeared in Scientific Reports in 2023. 4. Vargas Jr. et al. examined the role of epistasis in resistance to amikacin, kanamycin, bedaquiline, and clofazimine in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2021. 5. Li et al. utilized CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) chemical genetics and comparative genomics to identify genes mediating drug potency in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Nature Microbiology in 2022. 6. Yamamoto et al. demonstrated that the coexpression of MmpS5 and MmpL5 contributes to both the trimerization of the efflux transporter MmpL5 and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in mSphere in 2021. 7. Xu et al. investigated bedaquiline resistance mutations, their correlation with drug exposure, and their impact on the proteome of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2023. 8. Balasubramanian et al. characterized the bactericidal activity and mechanism of action of AZD5847, a novel oxazolidinone for tuberculosis treatment. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2014. 9. Zhang et al. identified mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis associated with reduced susceptibility to linezolid. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2016. 10. McNeil et al. isolated and characterized oxazolidinone-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in vitro. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2017. 11. Ismail et al. used in vitro approaches to generate Mycobacterium tuberculosis mutants resistant to bedaquiline, clofazimine, or linezolid and identified associated genetic variants. Their findings were published in Journal of Microbiological Methods in 2018. 12. Pi et al. characterized linezolid-resistance-associated mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). This study was published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2019. 13. Waller et al. demonstrated that the evolution of antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis is associated with collateral drug phenotypes. Their findings were published in Nature Communications in 2023. 14. Fujiwara et al. elucidated mechanisms of resistance to delamanid, a drug used for treating Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Tuberculosis (Edinburgh) in 2018. 15. Rifat et al. identified mutations in the fbiD (Rv2983) gene as a novel determinant of resistance to pretomanid and delamanid in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2020. 16. Wang et al. optimized antitubercular triazines and studied their intrabacterial metabolism. This study was published in Cell Chemical Biology in 2020. 17. Battaglia et al. characterized genomic variants associated with resistance to bedaquiline and delamanid in naïve clinical strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2020. 18. Mansjö et al. investigated resistance to delamanid and pretomanid in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, focusing on genetic determinants. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2022. 19. Lee et al. used protein engineering to predict nitroimidazole antibiotic resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in PLoS Pathogens in 2020. 20. Manson et al. conducted a genomic analysis of globally diverse Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains, providing insights into the emergence and spread of multidrug resistance. This study was published in Nature Genetics in 2017. 21. Domenech et al. experimentally confirmed that an uncommon rrs gene mutation (g878a) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis confers resistance to streptomycin. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2022. 22. Okamoto et al. demonstrated that the loss of a conserved 7-methylguanosine modification in 16S rRNA confers low-level streptomycin resistance in bacteria. This study was published in Molecular Microbiology in 2007. 23. Wong et al. identified mutations in the gidB gene that confer low-level streptomycin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2011. 24. Cohen et al. provided evidence supporting the expanded role of streptomycin in managing drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2020. 25. Vilchèze and Jacobs reviewed the genetic basis of resistance to isoniazid and ethionamide in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, focusing on genes, mutations, and causative mechanisms. Their findings were published in Microbiology Spectrum in 2014. 26. Grant et al. identified Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenases EthA and MymA as essential for activating inhibitors of replicating and non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Cell Chemical Biology in 2016. 27. Lefford and Mitchison compared methods for testing the sensitivity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to ethionamide. Their findings were published in Tubercle in 1966. 28. Cambau et al. revisited susceptibility testing in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) using a standardized quantitative phenotypic assessment in a European multicenter study. This study was published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2015. 29. Rueda et al. conducted a genotypic analysis of genes associated with independent resistance and cross-resistance to isoniazid and ethionamide in clinical isolates of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2015. 30. Matrat et al. performed a functional analysis of DNA gyrase mutant enzymes carrying mutations at position 88 in the A subunit, found in clinical strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistant to fluoroquinolones. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2006. 31. Nimmo et al. investigated bedaquiline resistance in drug-resistant tuberculosis patients co-infected with HIV. Their findings were published in European Respiratory Journal in 2020. 32. Modlin et al. described the atypical genetic basis of pyrazinamide resistance in monoresistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2021. 33. Nakatani et al. explored the role of alanine racemase mutations in D-cycloserine resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2017. 34. Fitzgibbon et al. reported false detection of rifampicin resistance using the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay due to an A451V mutation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in JAC Antimicrobial Resistance in 2021. 35. Zhang et al. identified Rv1453 as a gene associated with clofazimine resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Microbiology Spectrum in 2023. 36. Merker et al. characterized phylogenetically informative mutations in genes implicated in antibiotic resistance in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. This study was published in Genome Medicine in 2020. 37. Abrahams et al. identified DprE2 as a molecular target of the anti-tubercular nitroimidazole compounds pretomanid and delamanid. Their findings were published in Nature Communications in 2023. 38. Antoine et al. provided bioinformatic evidence for gene disruption caused by IS6110 in clinical Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains, leading to undiagnosed antibiotic resistance. This study was published in Microbiology Spectrum in 2021. 39. Roberts et al. demonstrated that repeated evolution of bedaquiline resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis is driven by truncation of the mmpR5 gene. This study was published in bioRxiv in 2022. 40. Siu et al. identified an upstream truncation of the furA-katG operon that confers high-level isoniazid resistance in a clinical isolate of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with no known resistance-associated mutations. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2014. 41. Liu et al. reviewed the role of synonymous codon usage in regulating gene expression and protein folding. Their findings were published in Annual Review of Biochemistry in 2021. 42. Rodriguez et al. demonstrated that synonymous codon substitutions regulate transcription and translation of an upstream gene. This study was published in bioRxiv in 2022. 43. Hegelmeyer et al. showed that gene recoding by synonymous mutations creates promiscuous intragenic transcription initiation in mycobacteria. This study was published in bioRxiv in 2023. 44. Yadon et al. comprehensively characterized PncA polymorphisms that confer resistance to pyrazinamide. Their findings were published in Nature Communications in 2017. 45. Omar et al. highlighted systematic rifampicin resistance errors with the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay and discussed implications for genotypic assay regulation. This study was published in International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2020. 46. Ocheretina et al. examined the impact of bacillary load on the accuracy of rifampicin resistance results using the Xpert MTB/RIF assay. Their findings were published in International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2021. 47. Rigouts et al. evaluated the performance of the GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay in detecting uncommon rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in BMC Research Notes in 2023. 48. Blakemore and Alland described diagnostic inconsistencies observed with an obsolete version of the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, which are unlikely to recur in the current version. This study was published in Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2014. 49. Hunt et al. introduced Minos, a tool for variant adjudication and joint genotyping of bacterial genome cohorts. Their findings were published in Genome Biology in 2022. 50. Rausch et al. developed DELLY, a tool for structural variant discovery using integrated paired-end and split-read analysis. This study was published in Bioinformatics in 2012. 51. The Seq&Treat initiative focuses on next-generation tuberculosis care, providing resources for sequencing and treatment strategies. 52. The WHO technical manual provides guidelines for drug susceptibility testing of medicines used in tuberculosis treatment. 53. Noncommercial culture and drug-susceptibility testing methods are recommended for screening patients at risk for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, as outlined in a policy statement. 54. Martin et al. evaluated the Hardy TB MODS Kit™ for rapid phenotypic diagnosis of tuberculosis and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. This study was published in PLoS One in 2014. 55. Guidelines for drug susceptibility testing of second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs for DOTS-Plus programs are available through WHO resources. 56. Policy guidance on drug susceptibility testing (DST) of second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs is provided by the WHO. 57. The companion handbook to the WHO guidelines for programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis offers additional resources for implementation. 58. Torre et al. highlighted the variable ability of rapid tests to detect rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that confer phenotypically occult rifampicin resistance. This study was published in Scientific Reports in 2019. 59. Verboven et al. introduced TBProfiler, an automated tool for identifying variants associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in PLoS One in 2022. 60. Zhang et al. elucidated the molecular basis for the exquisite sensitivity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to isoniazid. This study was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA in 1996. 61. Hicks et al. identified mutations in dnaA and a cryptic interaction site that increase drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in PLoS Pathogens in 2020. 62. Vilchèze et al. demonstrated that mycothiol biosynthesis is essential for ethionamide susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Molecular Microbiology in 2008. 63. Vilchèze et al. mapped coresistance to isoniazid and ethionamide to mycothiol biosynthetic genes in Mycobacterium bovis. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2011. 64. Green et al. used a convolutional neural network to highlight mutations relevant to antimicrobial resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study was published in Nature Communications in 2022. 65. Hicks et al. identified clinically prevalent mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that alter drug resistance phenotypes. This study was published in PLoS Pathogens in 2020.
